transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-11-04
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Reed (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Northfield VP Eng), Samir Khan (Security Architect), Priya Mehta (Eng Manager)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough): Quick security intake - focus on KMS, SSO, retention. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictability but wants proof of isolation and auditability.

Topics: SOC2/ISO baseline, SSO/SAML onboarding, RBAC mapping from IDP, encryption options (CMK vs Redwood-managed), audit logs format and retention windows, private VPC deployment constraints.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes blocked. Quick round robin — I'm Maya, AE, and with me is Connor, our solutions engineer.
[00:00:12] Connor: Hi all. Hi. Um yeah, happy to dig into infra, keys, logs — whatever you want.
[00:00:18] Lena: Hey Maya, hi Connor. I'm Lena, VP Engineering. Samir's our security architect, and Priya runs the teams using the models.
[00:00:26] Samir: Thanks. Quick note — we're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary gating items are KMS ownership, SSO integration, audit log retention and clarity, and evidence of SOC2/ISO controls.
[00:00:40] Maya: Great, that's exactly what we wanted to cover. Connor, want to start with KMS/crypto?
[00:00:46] Connor: Sure. So, Redwood provides three common paths — hosted with Redwood-managed keys, hosted with customer-managed CMKs via cloud KMS integrations, and Private (VPC/on-prem) where keys remain in your HSM. In practice, for Dedicated we typically allow BYOK via cloud KMS — redwood will call your KMS for envelope keys. There's also an option for customer-managed HSM in Private deployments.
[00:01:10] Priya: When you say "call your KMS" — is that direct network egress from the inference pods, or do you proxy through Redwood control plane? We have strict egress rules so that is important.
[00:01:21] Connor: Good question. For Hosted with CMK we do a secure call from the execution nodes to your KMS — it's outbound to the KMS endpoint, and we can put that through a dedicated NAT/IP allowlist. For Private deployments the KMS is on-prem or in customer's VPC so no public egress. I should flag that our Hosted flow can be configured to limit egress and lock IPs, but it's not the same as on-prem HSM.
[00:01:44] Samir: Ok, we need to validate the IP ranges and the proof that keys are never exfiltrated. Any artifacts on key rotation and KMS audit events?
[00:01:53] Maya: Yes, we'll share our KM docs and a redacted sample of KMS audit events. We have rotation cadence documented and we support rotation without downtime via envelope keys.
[00:02:02] Connor: Also note — for Dedicated we run customer-isolated GPU pools; that gives you logical separation, dedicated tenancy. For Private you'd get completely isolated control plane and no Redwood-hosted key material.
[00:02:12] Lena: That helps. Next — SSO. We use Okta with SAML and SCIM for user provisioning, and we need RBAC mapping so our identity groups map to Redwood roles for models/route access.
[00:02:25] Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. Connor, can you cover the mapping?
[00:02:30] Connor: Yeah. Onboarding, we map SAML assertions groups to Redwood roles. We support default roles and also custom role definitions; SCIM creates users and group membership so you can manage group membership centrally. There are a couple of gotchas — group attribute names differ across IdPs and sometimes our automated mapping needs a small script.
[00:02:47] Priya: When a user is deprovisioned, how quickly is access revoked — is there a TTL?
[00:02:52] Connor: SCIM immediate provisioning/deprovisioning is near real-time — deprovision events are reflected within a minute or two. Token lifetimes for active sessions depend on session config, but we can set session TTLs to meet your SSO policy.
[00:03:05] Samir: We also need role-level audit trails — who called which model, which key was used, request metadata — must be exportable for our SIEM.
[00:03:14] Maya: Our audit logs include request metadata, model id, route id, token usage, timestamps, and audit events like auth grants. We'll share a sample schema. Connor: format and retention?
[00:03:24] Connor: Logs are JSON-lines by default, with structured fields. For Hosted we retain logs for 90 days, with options for longer retention via log-export to your S3 or SIEM. For Dedicated and Private we can increase retention and deliver to customer-managed sinks — S3, Splunk, or SIEM via forwarders.
[00:03:40] Lena: 90 days by default — we need 2 years for audit, but we're ok if we can export to our S3 and enforce lifecycle there. Is export automated?
[00:03:49] Connor: Yes, we have an automated export where logs are pushed to a customer-owned S3 bucket daily; lifecycle and retention are then yours to control. For Dedicated we can also support streaming in near real-time.
[00:04:00] Priya: Is there PII scrubbing in logs or do logs contain raw prompts and outputs? That is critical.
[00:04:07] Connor: By default logs include prompt metadata and truncated text for debugging. We offer configurable scrubbing pipelines — you can opt out of storing prompt/output bodies, store only hashes, or apply redaction rules. For Private deployments customers often choose to never persist prompts centrally.
[00:04:22] Samir: Ok, that sounds promising. Next — SOC2/ISO evidence. We need SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 artifact copies, and a mapping to our control framework.
[00:04:32] Maya: We maintain SOC2 Type II reports and ISO27001 certs, plus a compliance pack that maps controls. I'll attach the redacted Type II and certs in the follow-up.
[00:04:40] Lena: Great — can you also include names of sub-processors and data center regions? We have data residency constraints for EU workloads.
[00:04:47] Maya: Yes, sub-processor list and regions will be in the pack. For Hosted we can pin region selection; for Dedicated we can provision in your preferred region subject to capacity.
[00:04:57] Priya: On data residency — if we use Hosted but select EU region, what about backups and logs? Are backups replicated outside region?
[00:05:05] Connor: Backups and logs for region-pinned tenants remain in-region by default. For some managed services there are control-plane touches that may cross region — we'll detail that in the doc.
[00:05:14] Samir: About RBAC — can we federate authorization for API keys? We have machine users and service accounts and want fine-grained RBAC for route-level controls.
[00:05:24] Connor: Yes. We have API key scoping and token-level permissions. You can create service accounts with scopes limited to specific models and routes. For more advanced use, we support short-lived tokens via your STS integration.
[00:05:36] Lena: That's good. We need an approval flow for who can spin up new model routes — change control is audited.
[00:05:42] Maya: We have admin workflows and approval roles documented; we also emit admin-approval audit events. We'll share a sample.
[00:05:49] Priya: Curious about encryption at rest — are model weights encrypted, and are cached KV stores encrypted?
[00:05:56] Connor: Model weights at rest are encrypted. KV caches and disk-backed caches are also encrypted at rest. For Hosted, disk encryption keys are managed by Redwood unless you supply CMKs. For Dedicated and Private you can bring your own keys.
[00:06:09] Samir: Can we get proof that keys are not accessible to Redwood operators in the BYOK case?
[00:06:15] Connor: In BYOK with cloud KMS, Redwood never stores the plaintext key — we perform envelope encryption and the KMS does the unwrap. We can provide architecture diagrams and sample key access logs showing that unwraps are initiated from execution nodes and are authorized by your KMS. For on-prem HSM, keys never leave your network.
[00:06:33] Lena: Excellent. Now, latency/cost tradeoff — we're leaning to Dedicated for predictable latency but concerned about cost. Can Redwood do a pilot in Dedicated with limited capacity?
[00:06:42] Maya: We do pilot Dedicated proofs — usually a month-long reserved pool at a reduced rate for trial. Connor: from a technical side we can allocate a small GPU pool and run your traffic patterns for smoke testing.
[00:06:52] Connor: Also, caching and batching config can drastically change unit cost — we can run a perf sketch against your prompt distribution.
[00:06:59] Priya: We'll send sample query distribution — average tokens and 95th pct lengths.
[00:07:05] Samir: One more — retention of training data. We plan to use outputs for later fine-tuning; however, some customers require that inputs be excluded from logs used for training. What's Redwood policy?
[00:07:16] Maya: We don't use customer data to train public models by default. For Hosted, customers can opt in or out of data usage. For Dedicated and Private, data never leaves the tenancy unless you configure sharing. We'll include a doc section on data usage and opt-outs.
[00:07:30] Priya: Good. Ok, some nitty gritty — audit log schema example?
[00:07:34] Connor: I'll paste a schema in follow-up but it's JSON-lines with fields: timestamp, request_id, model_id, route_id, user_id, service_account, api_key_hash, response_size, latency_ms, keystore_key_id (if used), auth_event. There can be prompt_hash or prompt_truncated depending on config.
[00:07:51] Samir: We need logs forwarded to our SIEM with guaranteed delivery and acking — can you guarantee at-least-once?
[00:07:57] Connor: For Dedicated we have delivery pipelines with retries; near real-time streaming will have at-least-once semantics. For Hosted exported daily batches we guarantee delivery and have MD5/s3 acking. We'll document delivery SLAs.
[00:08:11] Lena: Sounds like we have a path. A couple of edge constraints — we have an internal compliance checklist that requires the vendor to support encrypted logs at rest, support for customer KMS, and SAML provisioning. Those look covered.
[00:08:23] Maya: Great. Anything else on retention windows?
[00:08:26] Priya: One point — we may need ephemeral retention for predictions (like discard after 24 hours) except for flagged debug windows. Can you support short TTLs?
[00:08:35] Connor: Yes, you can configure retention per-route: immediate discard, short TTL (24h), or long-term (customer-managed S3). We'll note that route-level TTLs can affect caching effectiveness.
[00:08:47] Samir: And can we periodically run integrity checks against logs — like tamper-evident sequencing? We need chain-of-custody.
[00:08:55] Connor: We support signed log bundles and can provide periodic checksums. For higher assurance, Private deployments let you manage signatures directly.
[00:09:04] Maya: Ok, I'll recap outstanding asks. We'll share: SOC2/ISO artifacts, sub-processor list, KMS architecture diagrams, sample audit log schema and redacted logs, options on SSO/SCIM mapping, and a Dedicated pilot proposal with pricing sketch.
[00:09:18] Lena: Good. Timeline wise, we want to decide by the end of November. Pilot needs to start mid-November if possible.
[00:09:25] Maya: We'll aim to get docs out by Monday, 2027-11-06, and Connor will send the perf/cost sketch by 11/09. Can we tentatively set the infra workshop for 2027-11-10?
[00:09:36] Lena: That works for us. Samir will bring network and KMS folks to that session.
[00:09:40] Samir: Yep.
[00:09:42] Priya: Quick logistics — who should we add to the calendar for the infra workshop?
[00:09:46] Maya: Add me and Connor, and cc security@redwood.com, I'll send the invite after I share the docs.
[00:09:53] Samir: One last clarify — can you confirm whether your audit logs include model outputs if we disable prompt storage? We want outputs off by default.
[00:10:01] Connor: If you disable prompt/storage we can omit both prompt and full output bodies from the logs; you can keep hashes for debugging. We'll be explicit in the follow-up.
[00:10:10] Lena: Thanks, that was helpful. Quick recap and next steps?
[00:10:14] Maya: Recap: send security pack and artifacts, do perf/cost sketch, schedule infra workshop 11/10, customer to share retention policy and traffic samples. Action items noted in follow-up.
[00:10:24] Priya: Perfect.
[00:10:26] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and calendar.
[00:10:30] Connor: Thanks all.
[00:10:32] Lena: Thanks.

(There is some crosstalk at 00:10:35 - audio drop; transcript may have mis-heard a couple of technical terms e.g., "KV cache" heard as "KV case")

End of call.

Notes on quality: Some proper nouns/transcription of product names may be slightly off; timestamps are approximate.
